note.note:
Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  - Dysuria (burning/stinging on passing urine), increased urinary frequency, lower abdominal ache; onset after first trying cannabis ~1.5 weeks ago noted by patient but clinician considered this likely unrelated.
  - Patient reports noticing pink discoloration of urine today (possible hematuria).
- Symptom timeline and progression:
  - Symptoms present for just under a week (patient corrected initial “few days” to ~<1 week).
  - Burning with urination and increased frequency ongoing; lower abdominal aching worse with voiding.
- ENT symptoms:
  - None reported (no throat tightness, voice change, dysphagia, drooling, nasal/ocular symptoms, stridor, dyspnea, facial/lip/tongue/uvula swelling, ear pain, or neck swelling).
- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  - No prior similar episodes documented.
  - History of IBS with intermittent bowel habit variability.
  - No prior hospitalizations or emergency injections reported.
- Allergies and current medications:
  - Allergy: Clindamycin — adverse reaction unspecified.
  - Regular medications: combined oral contraceptive pill (type not specified; dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - IBS medication described as starting with “M” but exact name not specified; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Any relevant social context:
  - Lives in university halls with a flatmate; family live outside London.
  - Smoked cannabis once ~1.5 weeks ago (not a regular smoker); drinks alcohol socially.
  - Not currently sexually active with others outside long-term boyfriend; last unprotected intercourse approximately 1 week ago.
  - Last menstrual period two weeks ago (clinician noted pregnancy as low likelihood but to bear in mind if no improvement).

Objective:
- Observable swelling/distribution: Not recorded / no swelling reported.
- Airway/breathing descriptors: Not recorded / no respiratory symptoms reported.
- Mental status and associated features: Alert, no dizziness or syncope reported.
- Vitals and examination findings: Not recorded. Clinician did not perform physical examination during this remote consult.
- Presence of another person with the patient: Not recorded.

Assessment:
- Primary impression: Suspected lower urinary tract infection / acute cystitis.
  - Justification: Typical dysuria, urinary frequency, lower abdominal suprapubic ache, recent onset (~<1 week), and pink discoloration of urine reported today.
  - No systemic features to suggest upper urinary tract involvement (no fever, no flank/back pain, no vomiting reported).
- Differential/considerations noted by clinician: pregnancy considered low likelihood due to combined pill and recent period but to bear in mind if no improvement.
- Conflict noted:
  - Initial timeline stated as “a few days” by clinician; patient later clarified duration as just under one week.

Plan:
- Immediate actions advised/taken:
  - Arrange for patient to provide a urine sample: patient to come to practice and drop off a sample for testing and laboratory culture.
  - Start antibiotics advised (options discussed): Trimethoprim — dose/route/frequency not documented; Nitrofurantoin (three-day course mentioned) — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Advise hydration and oral analgesia for pain (Paracetamol recommended; dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Specific instructions to patient:
  - Provide urine sample at the practice as arranged; results will be sent to lab and clinician will contact patient with results.
  - Remain vigilant for worsening symptoms.
  - If symptoms not improving within one week, return for review.
- Escalation criteria / red flags (explicitly advised):
  - Call clinician / practice if fever, back pain (flank pain), or vomiting develop.
  - Seek prompt review if symptoms worsen or fail to improve.
- Follow-up:
  - Re-assessment if not improved in one week.
  - Laboratory urine culture results to guide antibiotic choice and further management; clinician will contact patient with results.
  - No ENT or allergy referral indicated from this consult.
- Other counseling:
  - Clinician advised general avoidance of cannabis use moving forward for health reasons.
  - Pregnancy considerations noted (last period two weeks ago); no pregnancy testing arranged in this consult.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vital signs (temperature, HR, BP) not recorded.
  - Urine dipstick / microscopy results and urine culture pending (no current results).
  - No physical pelvic or abdominal exam performed (remote consult).
  - No detailed description of the allergic reaction to clindamycin (type/severity) — important for future antibiotic choices.
  - Exact name and dosing of IBS medication not documented.
  - Exact antibiotic prescription (choice, dose, route, duration) not documented.
  - No pregnancy test documented despite recent unprotected intercourse and recent period two weeks ago.
- Internal conflicts from the transcript:
  - Duration of symptoms: initially described as “a few days” by clinician vs patient clarification of “just under a week” (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality:
  - Overall reasonably clear audio; a few drug/word pronunciations were unclear (IBS medication name only partially recalled by patient; clindamycin pronunciation slightly uncertain).
